newsitem.title: ITALY: Magistrate orders fast-track trial for Fiat chief.
newsitem.headline: Magistrate orders fast-track trial for Fiat chief.

text.p: A Turin magistrate said on Thursday that Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti and Finance Director Francesco Paolo Mattioli would stand trial for alleged balance sheet falsification on January 15.
Examining magistrate Francesco Saluzzo ordered the trial, under a special fast-track procedure in response to a request by lawyers acting for Romiti and Mattioli.
Magistrates asked last year for the two men to be sent for trial on charges of accounting and tax fraud and making illegal payments.

The officials are accused of diverting more than 30 billion lire ($19.8 million) into overseas accounts which were then allegedly used to make payments to political parties, politicians and Fiat managers working abroad.
Romiti took over the Fiat chairmanship in March from Giovanni Agnelli who stood down after 30 years at the helm. -- Milan newsroom +392-66102321 ($ = 1517 Italian Lire)
